description: A highly capable, feature-rich programming language.

tip: Signal the end of options; later arguments are treated as filenames and arguments.

option.name: --help
tip: Print a summary of the command-line options.

option.name: --version
tip: Print the Perl version and patchlevel.
Set the input record separator to an octal or hexadecimal number.
With no digits, the separator is the null character.
The value must be attached: 00 enables paragraph mode, and 0777 (or any value of 0400 or above) slurps whole files.
Hexadecimal form: -0xHHH, e.g. -0x1FF.

option.name: -a
tip: Turn on autosplit mode with -n or -p, splitting $_ into @F.
Implicitly sets -n.
Use -F to specify an alternate delimiter.

option.name: -c
tip: Check the syntax only, then exit without executing the program.
BEGIN, UNITCHECK, CHECK and use statements still run.

option.name: -C
tip: Control Perl's Unicode features with a number or a list of letters.
Letters: I (stdin), O (stdout), E (stderr), S (all three), i (input layer), o (output layer), D (both layers), A (@ARGV), L (locale-conditional), a (UTF-8 cache debugging).
The value must be attached; -C alone is equivalent to -CSDL and -C0 disables all features.

option.name: -d
tip: Run the program under the Perl debugger.
Append t for the threaded debugger.
Attach :MOD immediately to use Devel::MOD, e.g. -d:DProf.

option.name: -D
tip: Set debugging flags as a bit mask or a list of letters.
The value must be attached, e.g. -Dtls or -Dx.
Only a perl built with DEBUGGING uses these flags; other builds warn instead.

option.name: -dt
tip: Run the program under the threaded Perl debugger.
Sets PERL5DB_THREADED=1.
Attach :MOD immediately to use Devel::MOD instead.

option.name: -e
tip: Supply one line of program on the command line.
May be repeated; when -e is given, no program file is read.

option.name: -E
tip: Supply one line of program on the command line, like -e but with all optional features and builtins enabled.
May be repeated; when -E is given, no program file is read.

option.name: -f
tip: Skip executing $Config{sitelib}/sitecustomize.pl at startup.

option.name: -F
tip: Set the split() pattern for -a.
The pattern may be wrapped in //, "" or ''.
The value must be attached, and it implicitly sets -a and -n.

option.name: -g
tip: Slurp input by undefining the input record separator.
Alias for -0777.

option.name: -i
tip: Edit files processed by <> in place.
The extension must be attached and creates a backup copy; without one the original is discarded.
A * in the extension is replaced by the filename.

option.name: -I
tip: Prepend a directory to @INC, the module search path.
May be repeated.

option.name: -l
tip: Enable line-ending processing.
With -n or -p, chomp the input record separator and set the output record separator to octnum, which defaults to $/.
The value must be attached.

option.name: -m
tip: Execute use module () before the program, loading it without calling import.
The module name may be attached or passed as the next argument.

option.name: -M
tip: Execute use module before the program, loading it and calling import.
Use -Mmodule=arg1,arg2 to import symbols.
Prefix the module with - to call no instead of use.
The module name may be attached or passed as the next argument.

option.name: -n
tip: Assume a while (<>) { ... } loop around the program.
Use -p to print each line as well.

option.name: -p
tip: Assume a while (<>) { ... } loop that prints each line, like sed.

option.name: -s
tip: Enable rudimentary parsing of switches after the program file.
Each switch sets a variable in the main package; use is discouraged.

option.name: -S
tip: Search PATH for the program file unless its name contains a path separator.

option.name: -t
tip: Enable taint checks as warnings instead of fatal errors.
Use -T for real taint checks in production code.

option.name: -T
tip: Turn on taint checks.
Must appear early on the command line.

option.name: -u
tip: Dump core after compiling the program.
Intended for use with the undump utility.

option.name: -U
tip: Allow unsafe operations, such as unlinking directories while running as superuser.

option.name: -V
tip: Print a summary of the major Perl configuration values and the current @INC.
Attach :configvar immediately to print a single Config.pm variable, e.g. -V:libc.
The configvar may be a regex, and extra colons control the formatting.

option.name: -w
tip: Enable warnings about dubious constructs.

option.name: -W
tip: Enable all warnings, regardless of no warnings or $^W.

option.name: -x
tip: Ignore leading garbage until a #! line containing "perl".
Attach a directory immediately to chdir into it before running the program.
The directory must follow -x with no whitespace.

option.name: -X
tip: Disable all warnings, regardless of use warnings or $^W.
